nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model (HBLM) with site as a random effect; Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model (HBGPM) adding a Gaussian process for age.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In a hierarchical linear version of the model, site is modeled hierarchically, resulting in a random effect for site ('Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model, HBLM'). In a non-linear version of the model, a Gaussian Process for age is added to test whether performance is increased if the model is also able to capture non-linear effects between age and thickness of the cortical region ('Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model, HBGPM').
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Bayer2022.pdf.md: Section 3.4 Site as a predictor in a Hierarchical Bayesian Model

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness of 34 bilateral regions and average cortical thickness.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For the current study, we focused on cortical thickness measures of the 34 bilateral regions (averaged between left and right hemisphere) of the Desikian Killiany atlas parcellation... and the average cortical thickness across all 34 regions.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was used as the primary predictor (fixed effect) for modeling cortical thickness trajectories. In the HBGPM model, age was modeled non-linearly using a Gaussian Process. Sex was included as a covariate in the models to preserve biological variation of interest. Site was included as a random effect in the hierarchical Bayesian models to account for scanner/acquisition differences across the 17 sites in the ABIDE dataset.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We compared the performance of a linear and a non-linear hierarchical Bayesian model in modeling the effect of age on cortical thickness; An overview of the distribution of age and sex for the training and test sets for healthy controls and individuals with autism can be found in Fig. 2; The ability of the model to deal with site effects is obtained by introducing a random effect for site s = 1, 2, . . . ,q so that the prediction for the i th subject is a combination of fixed and varying effects; We propose a hierarchical Bayesian approach in which we include site as a random effect in the model
